questions.question: What is the N+1 problem?
options: One query loads N parents and then N more queries load their children
A table needs N+1 columns to store a relationship
A transaction runs N+1 times after a rollback
A repository has N+1 methods with the same name
questions.explanation: One query for the list plus one query per row for the related data gives N+1 queries.

questions.question: Which change reduces N+1 by loading parents and children in a single query?
questions.explanation: JOIN FETCH and @EntityGraph tell JPA to load the children in the same query as the parents.

questions.question: A page loads 20 wards with findAll() and then calls ward.getPatients().size() for each one. The patients collection is lazy. How many SQL statements run?
questions.explanation: One statement loads the 20 wards and each lazy patients collection runs its own statement, so 1 + 20 = 21.

questions.question: To remove N+1, a developer changes the patients collection to FetchType.EAGER and still calls findAll(). What is the problem?
options: Eager collections cannot be used with Set
findAll() still runs extra queries per parent, and now children load even when not needed
Hibernate refuses to start the application
questions.explanation: EAGER does not turn findAll() into a join, so the extra queries remain and every use of the entity gets heavier.

questions.question: A @Query uses JOIN FETCH on two List collections of the same entity and Hibernate throws MultipleBagFetchException. What is a safe fix?
options: Fetch one collection with JOIN FETCH and use @BatchSize for the other
questions.explanation: Fetching two bags in one join is not allowed, so join one collection and load the other with batch fetching.
